result.process_description:
If goods shall be shipped, the secretary clarifies who will do the shipping. 
If you have large amounts, special shipping will be necessary. 
In these cases the secretary invites three logistic companies to make offers and she selects one of them. 
In case of small amounts, normal post shipment is used. 
Therefore a package label is written by the secretary and a parcel insurance taken by the logistics department head if necessary. 
In the meantime the goods can be already packaged by the warehousemen. 
If everything is ready, the packaged goods are prepared for being picked up by the logistic company.

args.text: When the description mentions an outside organization only as the recipient of an invitation or request, without describing its own process or response activities, model the interaction within the existing process rather than adding a separate participant pool and message flow.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers when an external organization should be modeled as a separate pool.

result.rule: Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Do not attach message flows to lanes, gateways, data objects, groups or annotations; use participant boundaries or eligible flow nodes.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.

args.text: When a process description mentions an outside organization only as the recipient of an invitation or request, and describes no activities or response from that organization, keep the invitation or request within the described participant's process rather than adding a separate pool and message flow.

trace.reason: Check whether an error-driven guideline already covers this collaboration modeling choice.

result.rule: When the description says that a process may continue only after an external participant approves a proposal: Model the approval wait as an intermediate catch event after the proposal is provided and before the dependent activity; preserve that order rather than modeling the wait as a task.

When the description states that one participant requests information or action from another participant and that the other participant provides a response: Model the request and response as a connected interaction: use sequence flows within a participant’s process and message flows between distinct participant pools, rather than an unrelated detached start-to-end chain.

When the description assigns work to multiple internal roles or departments within one process and also describes interaction with an outside participant: Model the internal responsibilities as lanes within the same process pool; model the outside participant separately only when the description establishes independent communication.

When the description states that an external participant performs an action that initiates work by another participant: Model the action as a task in the external participant’s process and connect it to the receiving participant’s process with a message flow.

args.text: When the description mentions outside organizations as recipients of a request or invitation, but does not describe an independently scoped process for them, model the request within the described participant's process rather than creating a separate pool and message flow.
